blueprints.title: Teeth, gums & periodontal attachment
blueprints.query: tooth regeneration periodontal ligament gingival stem cells functional comparator
blueprints.question: Which components of a bioidentical tooth and its supporting tissues have direct functional evidence, and what remains missing?
blueprints.who: Keep human trials, human-derived constructs in mice and embryonic mouse tooth-germ studies separate.
blueprints.what: Enamel, dentin, living pulp, cementum, periodontal ligament, alveolar bone and gingival barrier as distinct outcomes.
blueprints.where: Restore the tooth-root/ligament/bone interface and gingival seal; avoid conflating bone fill with attachment.
blueprints.when: Development, eruption, early healing, loading and long-term durability are separate intervals.
blueprints.why: A calcified deposit or improved radiograph does not establish a complete innervated, load-bearing replacement tooth.
blueprints.how: Compare primary sources, intended tissue identity, controlled functional outcomes, adverse healing and donor/site dependence. Retain inconclusive and negative comparisons.
blueprints.falsifier: Mineral deposition without native-like architecture, ankylosis instead of ligament attachment, loss under load, impaired gum barrier or no advantage over the declared comparator.
blueprints.desired_changes: Build a component-level roadmap toward bioidentical tooth and periodontal restoration without upgrading partial endpoints to whole-organ regeneration.

blueprints.title: Organoids & stem-cell construct function
blueprints.query: organoid stem cell functional maturation oxygen profile independent donor validation
blueprints.question: Does a specified stem-cell construct reproduce a useful tissue function beyond morphology and marker expression?
blueprints.who: Declare species, donor, clone, culture and assay hierarchy; cultured human cells are not treated patients.
blueprints.what: Cell identity, maturation, transport, genome stability and tissue-specific function, measured independently.
blueprints.where: Local oxygen and nutrient transport, host interfaces and spatial organization.
blueprints.when: Formation, maturation, transplantation and persistence remain separate intervals.
blueprints.why: A reproducible image or marker panel does not establish useful organ function or transplant integration.
blueprints.how: Use source-qualified datasets, donor/culture-aware comparators and the independent organoid-oxygen-lab methods. Record model assumptions and measurement gaps.
blueprints.falsifier: Markers improve without function, construct selection explains the apparent effect, or transport/genome stability fails despite morphology.
blueprints.desired_changes: Connect qualified measurements to reproducible analyses while retaining organ-specific function and genome integrity as separate outcomes.

dental.label: Component identity and architecture
dental.prompt: Separate enamel, dentin, pulp, cementum, ligament, bone and gingiva; state the measured component.

dental.label: Periodontal attachment
dental.prompt: Distinguish clinical attachment gain, bone fill and histological oriented cementum–ligament–bone attachment.

dental.label: Gingival barrier and root coverage
dental.prompt: Record root coverage, tissue phenotype, seal/barrier measurements and recurrent inflammation separately.

dental.label: Loading, occlusion and sensation
dental.prompt: Declare the mechanical or sensory assay; mineralization alone is not mastication.

dental.label: Pulp, vascular and neural integration
dental.prompt: Record living pulp, vascular supply and innervation without inferring these from a mineral image.

dental.label: Adverse healing and ectopic outcomes
dental.prompt: Retain ankylosis, root resorption, abnormal tooth number/shape, ectopic mineralization and immune findings.

dental.label: Durability
dental.prompt: Record follow-up and performance under repeated loading.

dental.label: Comparator and independent unit
dental.prompt: Distinguish patients, teeth, sites, animals and cultures; identify primary versus post hoc outcomes.

organoids.label: Cell identity and maturation
organoids.prompt: Declare the cell composition and maturation assay.

organoids.label: Transport measurements
organoids.prompt: Separate measured local oxygen from gas settings and illustrative model parameters.

organoids.label: Tissue-specific function
organoids.prompt: Use a declared function beyond markers or morphology.

organoids.label: Genome integrity and clone behavior
organoids.prompt: Separate intended genetic correction, unwanted products and clonal selection.

organoids.label: Host integration
organoids.prompt: Track perfusion, innervation and anatomical interface where relevant.

organoids.label: Persistence and adverse outcomes
organoids.prompt: Record duration, attrition and adverse findings.

organoids.label: Source, comparator and independent unit
organoids.prompt: Preserve donor/clone/culture hierarchy and define the held-out unit.

dental.title: Whole-tooth function reference and adult-cell gap
dental.hypothesis: The mouse organ-germ result supplies a functional reference; adult-human cell sourcing and controlled tooth architecture remain independent gaps.
dental.endpoint: Hardness, loading response, sensory response, root/ligament integration and durability.
dental.falsifier: Mineralized tissue fails loading or lacks functional host integration.
dental.structure_notes: Source reports functional mouse tooth replacement. It does not establish an adult-human bioidentical tooth or an available adult-human cell source.

evidence.comparator: Native tooth and source-defined assays; verify each assay separately
evidence.notes: Abstract-reviewed functional precedent; no pooled human inference.

dental.title: Human ameloblast organoid enamel-like material
dental.tissue: Enamel-like material in a non-dental graft site
dental.hypothesis: Mature ameloblast organoids can produce a useful enamel component; native prism architecture, bonding and loading require separate tests.
dental.endpoint: Mineral composition/architecture, enamel–dentin interface, hardness and repeated-load behavior.
dental.falsifier: Calcified deposits lack appropriate architecture, adhesion or mechanical function.
dental.evidence_stage: Human iPSC organoid and mouse graft
dental.study_design: Mechanistic organoid study with kidney-capsule grafts
dental.structure_notes: The 2026 primary source reports enamel-like calcified material, not an erupted tooth. Its reported GEO accessions are dataset leads, not downloaded or qualified data here.

evidence.value: Ameloblast maturation and enamel-like calcified material
evidence.timepoint: Source-defined assays; no human replacement follow-up
evidence.notes: Publisher full text accessed; no complete periodontal unit or human benefit inferred.

dental.title: iPSC-derived PDL-like cells: reproducibility before integration
dental.target: Periodontal ligament-like cell source and construct qualification
dental.species: Human iPS-derived cells and donor-derived primary-cell comparators
dental.hypothesis: iPSC-derived PDL-like batches can reproduce selected PDL-associated markers, matrix and load responses; reproducibility across independent iPSC donors and interface function remain to be established.
dental.endpoint: Across independent iPSC lines and batches, predefined PDL identity/function markers, matrix response, mechanical response, oriented insertion at cementum and alveolar-bone interfaces, and residual-pluripotency/genomic-stability checks.
dental.falsifier: The phenotype fails across independent iPSC lines, drifts with passage, lacks oriented interface/load-transfer function, or retains unsafe pluripotent or genomic abnormalities.
dental.study_design: Compare iPS-PDL evidence with primary PDL donor cells; nest batches within their iPSC donor and technical replicates within batch. Require 3D interface and in-vivo evidence before efficacy claims.
dental.structure_notes: The 2026 study functionally characterized iPS-PDL cells from one iPSC line (HPS0381), using PDL-conditioned media from three preparations to generate three differentiation batches. Batches #2/#3 expressed more Asporin, TN-C and ALP than dermal fibroblasts; batch #1 was fibroblast-like for those markers. In-vitro osteogenic, matrix and compression responses were reported. No 3D construct, oriented insertion, transplantation or load transfer was tested. See studies/dental-regeneration-2026-10-09/IPS_PDL_FUNCTION_REVIEW.md. A complementary 2024 feeder-free iPDLSC study reported marker-positive bone/cementum-like tissue and collagen-I-positive PDL-like fibers after an 8-week ectopic subcutaneous mouse graft; its abstract omits graft n and iPSC-line identity, and it does not test tooth-site insertion or load transfer. See IPS_PDL_FUNCTION_REVIEW.md.

evidence.value: In-vitro PDL-like marker, matrix and mechanical-response signals were reported, but one of three differentiation batches resembled fibroblasts for selected markers.
evidence.unit: 3 batches, 1 iPSC line; assay replicates are not donors
evidence.comparator: Donor-derived primary PDL and dermal fibroblasts, depending on assay
evidence.notes: Supports a cell-source hypothesis, not a functional periodontal construct. Batch reproducibility and independent iPSC lines remain open.

evidence.value: An 8-week ectopic graft reportedly contained osteocalcin-positive bone/cementum-like tissue and collagen-I-positive PDL-like fibers.
evidence.comparator: On-feeder iPDLSCs for in-vitro marker context; no in-vivo comparator stated in abstract
evidence.notes: Subcutaneous location does not test tooth-site insertion or load transfer; graft denominator and iPSC-line identity are not stated in the retrieved abstract.

evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY 4.0; attributed summary
evidence_records.stage_track: In-vitro iPSC-derived periodontal ligament-like cell characterization
evidence_records.developmental_interval: Cell induction and early-passage in-vitro assays
evidence_records.model_system: iPS-PDL cells; marker, matrix, osteogenic and compressive-response assays
evidence_records.comparator: Skin fibroblasts for marker context; donor-derived primary PDL cells for doubling-time comparison
evidence_records.outcome: Selected PDL-associated features were observed in vitro, with differentiation-batch variability
evidence_records.measure: PDL-associated markers, mineralized matrix, ALP/collagen response, compressive-load response and cell doubling time
evidence_records.value: Three iPS-PDL batches from one iPSC line: batches #2/#3 exceeded dermal fibroblasts for Asporin, TN-C and ALP; batch #1 remained fibroblast-like for those markers. Osteogenic matrix/markers, AA-responsive ALP/collagen, and compression-induced IL6, IL1B and COX2 were reported. Doubling times were 15.73–24.48 h versus 44.60–59.96 h for primary PDL cells (p<0.01).
evidence_records.unit: In-vitro assays; three differentiation batches nested in one iPSC line; typically n=3 replicates, not independent donors
evidence_records.independent_unit: Three differentiation batches from the same iPSC line; not three independent iPSC donors. Three primary PDL donor lines were used in the growth comparison; technical replicates do not increase donor n.
evidence_records.sample_size: One iPSC line (HPS0381); three iPS-PDL batches generated with conditioned media from three PDL preparations; typically three assay replicates; three donor-derived PDL comparators for doubling time
evidence_records.follow_up: In vitro through passage 10 or earlier; no transplant follow-up
evidence_records.notes: Cell-characterization study only: no 3D ligament construct, oriented cementum/PDL/bone insertion, in-vivo integration, or load-transfer outcome. Authors note one iPSC line, batch variation, early passage, no comprehensive side-by-side primary-PDL validation, and need for genomic-stability, tumorigenicity and xeno-free safety assessment.

evidence_records.source_title: Feeder-free iPDLSC study 2024: ectopic mouse graft
evidence_records.license: Publisher abstract accessed; full text restricted in retrieved view; no full-text license claim made
evidence_records.species: Human iPSC-derived cells transplanted into immunodeficient mice
evidence_records.stage_track: Feeder-free iPSC-derived PDL-like cells and ectopic xenograft
evidence_records.model_system: Feeder-free iPSCs differentiated through neural-crest-like cells to PDL stem-cell-like cells; subcutaneous dorsal graft with β-tricalcium phosphate scaffold in immunodeficient mice
evidence_records.comparator: In-vitro marker expression compared with on-feeder iPDLSCs; no in-vivo comparator arm stated in the abstract
evidence_records.outcome: Marker-positive bone/cementum-like tissue and PDL-like fibers were reported in an ectopic graft
evidence_records.measure: Osteocalcin-positive tissue and collagen-I-positive fibers at 8 weeks
evidence_records.value: At 8 weeks, the abstract reports osteocalcin-positive bone/cementum-like tissues and collagen-I-positive PDL-like fibers
evidence_records.unit: Mouse ectopic graft; denominator not stated in the retrieved abstract
evidence_records.independent_unit: Animal/graft; denominator not stated in the retrieved abstract
evidence_records.sample_size: Not stated in the retrieved abstract; quantitative comparison awaits full-text assessment
evidence_records.notes: The graft was dorsal subcutaneous tissue, not a tooth socket. Marker-positive collagen fibers do not establish oriented insertion onto root cementum and alveolar bone, periodontal-space organization, physiologic mobility, or load transfer. The abstract does not identify the iPSC line or state the animal/graft denominator; do not infer donor-independent replication. Full text was restricted in the retrieved publisher view.

dental.title: Periodontal bone fill versus attachment benefit
dental.hypothesis: A cell-based construct may improve one outcome without an added attachment advantage over an active comparator.
dental.endpoint: Between-group clinical attachment, bone height, oriented attachment, mobility, adverse outcomes and follow-up.
dental.falsifier: Added cells do not improve the prespecified attachment endpoint or produce adverse integration.
dental.study_design: Contrast 2016 PDLSC trial, 2026 randomized ASC+PRP versus EMD trial, and 2025 pooled DPSC subgroup; separate bone, attachment, safety and histology endpoints.
dental.structure_notes: Full-text review: the 2026 trial found a 36-week radiographic bone-height signal for ASC+PRP versus EMD (difference 1.905 mm, 95% CI 0.383 to 3.427; p=0.0184; n=8 vs 6 at primary analysis). It reports no significant between-group CAL or probing-depth differences at 12/24/36 weeks; within-arm CAL change is not added benefit. Registry flow is 16 consented, one pre-treatment withdrawal, 15 treated (9 vs 6). The paper calls this therapeutic equivalence, but no margin/formal equivalence test is reported in Methods. No histology; bone fill does not establish oriented PDL. This is expanded adipose-derived cells + PRP, not PDLSCs or a whole tooth. Numeric supplements were unavailable, so no unreported contrasts are reconstructed. The 2016 and 2025 full-text records retain their endpoint-specific intervals and subgroup caveat.

evidence.value: 36-week radiographic bone-height difference 1.905 mm (95% CI 0.383 to 3.427; p=0.0184) favored ASC+PRP; no significant between-group CAL or probing-depth difference at 12, 24 or 36 weeks
evidence.unit: distinct outcomes: radiographic mm and clinical attachment/probing comparison
evidence.timepoint: 12, 24 and 36 weeks; primary bone-height analysis n=8 versus 6 at 36 weeks
evidence.notes: A positive bone-height proxy does not establish a clinical attachment advantage or oriented functional PDL. Exact secondary numeric contrasts unavailable. No formal equivalence margin/test is reported.

evidence.value: AE and SAE each 1/9 in ASC+PRP; acute periodontitis and heart failure in two different participants, judged unrelated by authors
evidence.unit: small-cohort participant count; imprecise safety estimate
evidence.notes: Official registry clarifies 16 consented, 1 withdrew before treatment, 15 treated. Small study cannot establish rare-event safety.

evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY 4.0; this record is an attributed summary
evidence_records.comparator: Cell group versus control with the shared regenerative treatment
evidence_records.outcome: Primary radiographic outcome: no significant between-group difference
evidence_records.value: Reported between-group p=0.742; both groups improved over time
evidence_records.unit: mm; source table labels mean +/- standard error
evidence_records.independent_unit: Teeth nested within patients; do not count teeth as independent patients
evidence_records.sample_size: 48 randomized teeth; 41 treated (20 cell, 21 control); 30 patients in the trial
evidence_records.notes: Full-text Methods and Table 2. Modified per-protocol analysis with last observation carried forward. Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence. Bone fill is a proxy, not functional ligament reconstruction.

evidence_records.source_title: PDLSC trial 2016: secondary clinical attachment outcome
evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY 4.0; this record is an attributed summary
evidence_records.outcome: Secondary clinical attachment comparison: no significant between-group difference
evidence_records.sample_size: 20 cell-group and 21 control-group teeth; not 41 independent patients
evidence_records.follow_up: 3 months for these clinical indices, not the 12-month radiographic interval
evidence_records.notes: Full-text efficacy assessment and Table 3. Retain this shorter outcome-specific interval. Clinical attachment level is not histologic proof of oriented cementum-ligament-bone attachment.

evidence_records.source_title: DPSC 2025: pooled post hoc stage-III attachment contrast
evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY 4.0; this record is an attributed summary
evidence_records.stage_track: Post hoc combined dataset from two trials
evidence_records.comparator: DPSC versus saline in the pooled post hoc subgroup
evidence_records.outcome: Attachment-loss change favored DPSC in this subgroup
evidence_records.measure: Table 3: day-180 AL change from baseline; DPSC minus saline
evidence_records.unit: mm; negative change denotes reduced attachment loss
evidence_records.independent_unit: Methods specify tooth-level statistical analysis; patient/site dependence requires review
evidence_records.sample_size: Table 3 group n=54 and 40; not asserted to be independently replicated patients
evidence_records.notes: Full-text Clinical outcomes and Table 3. Post hoc pooling across trials is not prespecified overall primary confirmation. Source CI/sign retained; no re-estimation without raw data or covariance. No histologic or mechanical attachment restoration is inferred.

evidence_records.source_title: ASC+PRP trial 2026: primary radiographic bone height at week 36
evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; attributed factual summary, no full-text excerpt
evidence_records.stage_track: Open-label randomized phase II periodontal trial
evidence_records.comparator: Autologous expanded adipose-derived stromal cells plus PRP versus enamel matrix derivative
evidence_records.outcome: Primary endpoint favored ASC+PRP for radiographic alveolar bone height
evidence_records.measure: Newly formed alveolar bone height at 36 weeks; Table 2
evidence_records.unit: mm; source-reported means +/- SD and between-group estimate
evidence_records.independent_unit: Participants randomized by trial arm; preserve patient as unit. Site-level dependency details are not available in retrieved main text.
evidence_records.sample_size: 36-week primary analysis: 8 ASC+PRP and 6 EMD participants; registry reports 9 and 6 treated
evidence_records.follow_up: Primary endpoint at 36 weeks after transplant
evidence_records.notes: Radiographic bone height is a proxy, not oriented cementum-periodontal-ligament-bone attachment. The study used expanded adipose-derived cells plus PRP, not PDLSCs; no ASC-only or PRP-only group. No histology was obtained. Small sample and larger observed than assumed SD limit precision.

evidence_records.source_title: ASC+PRP trial 2026: clinical attachment and probing depth
evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; attributed factual summary, no full-text excerpt
evidence_records.stage_track: Open-label randomized phase II periodontal trial
evidence_records.comparator: Autologous expanded adipose-derived stromal cells plus PRP versus enamel matrix derivative
evidence_records.outcome: No significant between-group difference in clinical attachment gain or probing-depth reduction
evidence_records.measure: Clinical attachment level and probing depth at 12, 24 and 36 weeks
evidence_records.value: Main text reports no significant between-group differences at any listed timepoint; ASC+PRP within-group CAL improved from baseline (p<0.01)
evidence_records.unit: mm; exact contrasts not reproduced because numeric supplement tables were unavailable
evidence_records.independent_unit: Participants randomized by trial arm; exact outcome-specific denominators and site-level dependence not available in retrieved main text.
evidence_records.sample_size: Trial treated 9 ASC+PRP and 6 EMD participants; exact CAL analysis denominators not reported in retrieved main text
evidence_records.follow_up: 12, 24 and 36 weeks; keep distinct from the 36-week primary radiographic endpoint
evidence_records.notes: Within-arm change is not an added benefit over EMD. The article describes therapeutic equivalence but the retrieved Methods give ordinary Student t-tests, without a stated equivalence margin or formal equivalence test. No equivalence conclusion is recorded.

evidence_records.source_title: ASC+PRP trial 2026: adverse events and registry flow
evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; attributed factual summary, no full-text excerpt
evidence_records.stage_track: Open-label randomized phase II periodontal trial
evidence_records.comparator: ASC+PRP safety cohort; participant flow cross-checked against official registry https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/latest-detail/jRCTb030190173
evidence_records.outcome: One adverse event and one serious adverse event were reported in the ASC+PRP arm; authors judged both unrelated to the procedure
evidence_records.value: Acute periodontitis and heart failure occurred in two different ASC+PRP participants; AE and SAE each 1/9 (11.1%), source-reported 95% CI 0.3% to 48.2%. Registry: 16 consented, 1 withdrew before treatment, 15 treated (9 ASC+PRP; 6 EMD).
evidence_records.sample_size: Safety denominator: 9 ASC+PRP treated participants; total treated 15
evidence_records.notes: Registry clarifies recruitment flow; this does not prove rare-event safety. One treated ASC+PRP participant is absent from the 36-week primary endpoint denominator (8 versus 9); the retrieved text does not state why. Separate AE and SAE counts should not be read as events in one person.

dental.title: Gingival coverage versus restored barrier
dental.species: Human clinical studies and follow-up; rabbit augmentation and canine recession models
dental.hypothesis: Cell adjuncts may alter coverage, early epithelialization or attachment morphology, but short-term root coverage alone may not produce a durable, functionally measured gum barrier.
dental.endpoint: Keep root coverage, epithelialization, functional seal, histologic attachment, inflammation and recurrence as separate outcomes.
dental.falsifier: A cell-containing approach fails to improve a prespecified independent barrier or durability endpoint over scaffold/surgery alone, or increases adverse healing.
dental.evidence_stage: Human clinical outcomes plus preclinical histology; endpoints and follow-up remain model-specific
dental.study_design: Compare 2017 and 2026 human cell-adjunct recession studies, 2021 rabbit early epithelialization, 2022 canine recession histology and 2019 long-term graft coverage; do not pool across models.
dental.structure_notes: The 2017 and 2026 human studies report six-month coverage outcomes but no functional epithelial-seal endpoint; the 2017 site totals conflict and the 2026 study includes only 10 men. Rabbit histology is a seven-day augmentation result. Canine recession histology shows both regenerative and long-junctional-epithelium repair patterns without a predictable cell-added effect. A 12-year graft follow-up is a durability benchmark, not cell-therapy evidence. Keep participants, sites, animals, histology and coverage distinct.

evidence.value: 2017 and 2026 human cell-adjunct studies report short-term root-coverage signals; neither measures epithelial-seal function
evidence.unit: Clinical root coverage and gingival phenotype; barrier function not directly measured
evidence.notes: Retain differing interventions, endpoints and the 2017 site-count discrepancy. The 2026 sample includes 10 men in a split-mouth design; no long-term recurrence endpoint.

evidence.value: Canine sections show both new attachment structures and long-junctional-epithelium repair; the cell-added histometric effect was not significant or predictable
evidence.unit: Short-term histology, separate from clinical root coverage and functional seal
evidence.comparator: CAF, collagen matrix, matrix plus GMSCs, and matrix plus fibroblasts
evidence.notes: Seven dogs and 56 tooth specimens; teeth are nested within animals. Does not establish a human result or load-bearing attachment.

evidence.value: Twelve-year graft follow-up found less reported root-coverage decline at grafted sites than adjacent CAF-only sites; no cell product was tested
evidence.unit: Mean root-coverage change over long follow-up
evidence.comparator: CAF+CTG, CAF+epithelial-collar graft and adjacent CAF-only sites
evidence.notes: Seventeen of 20 original participants and 43 sites; clinical coverage is not histology or a direct epithelial-seal test.

evidence_records.source_title: Zanwar et al. 2017: umbilical-cord-derived cells and polymer membrane
evidence_records.license: Primary article linked; this is an attributed summary without a source excerpt
evidence_records.stage_track: Small randomized clinical study of multiple gingival recessions
evidence_records.developmental_interval: Adult recession repair; baseline and six months
evidence_records.model_system: Multiple anterior Miller Class I/II gingival recession defects
evidence_records.comparator: Umbilical-cord-derived cells on PLA/PGA membrane versus PLA/PGA membrane without added cells
evidence_records.outcome: Mean root-coverage percentage favored the cell adjunct; other reported coverage and attachment contrasts were not significant
evidence_records.measure: Table 5 mean root coverage and complete root coverage; Table 4 recession reduction and clinical-attachment gain
evidence_records.value: Mean root coverage 66.26% versus 57.38% (reported p=.001); recession reduction 1.57±0.89 versus 1.24±0.47 mm (p=.35); attachment gain p=.92; complete root coverage p=.36
evidence_records.unit: Percent and mm; source-reported group summaries
evidence_records.independent_unit: Cases/patients with multiple recession sites; site counts conflict across article sections
evidence_records.sample_size: 14 reported cases; abstract/methods list 16 test and 14 control sites at baseline, while Results refer to 18 and 17 defects
evidence_records.notes: Preserve the reported mean root-coverage p-value alongside nonsignificant recession-depth reduction, attachment gain and complete-coverage results. The source's differing site totals limit interpretation. No epithelial-seal function or long-term recurrence was measured.

evidence_records.source_title: Sankar et al. 2026: autologous gingival fibroblasts on collagen matrix
evidence_records.license: Primary article linked; this is an attributed summary without a source excerpt
evidence_records.developmental_interval: Adult recession repair; baseline, one, three and six months
evidence_records.model_system: Selected Miller Class I/II recession sites
evidence_records.comparator: CAF plus volume-stable collagen matrix versus CAF plus autologous gingival-fibroblast-seeded matrix
evidence_records.outcome: Selected six-month clinical coverage measures favored the fibroblast side; secondary healing, esthetic and pain comparisons were not significant
evidence_records.measure: Six-month recession depth, recession width and clinical attachment level; Table 1 paired between-side comparisons
evidence_records.value: Test versus control: recession depth 0.1±0.32 versus 0.6±0.52 mm (p=.025); width 0 versus 0.8±0.63 mm (p=.011); attachment level 0.5±0.53 versus 1.5±0.53 mm (p=.008)
evidence_records.independent_unit: Ten participants in a split-mouth design; two sites per participant are paired, not independent patients
evidence_records.sample_size: 10 men and 20 sites; ten paired sites per treatment side
evidence_records.notes: Fibroblasts are not a characterized stem-cell population. The abstract calls CAL differences significant at all intervals, while the three-month Table 1 intergroup p-value is .053. Baseline plaque index is p=.046 despite narrative comparability, and no across-outcome multiplicity correction is described. No histology, epithelial-seal assay or recurrence endpoint.

evidence_records.source_title: Sánchez et al. 2022: canine recession histology with gingival MSCs
evidence_records.license: Primary article linked; this is an attributed summary without a source excerpt
evidence_records.model_system: Experimental recession defects treated with CAF, collagen matrix, matrix plus autologous GMSCs or matrix plus fibroblasts
evidence_records.outcome: Histology showed variable repair patterns across groups; the added GMSCs did not predictably shift healing toward the regenerative pattern
evidence_records.measure: Epithelial length, connective-tissue attachment, new cementum and bone on histologic sections
evidence_records.value: Some sections showed new cementum, bone and connective attachment; others showed long junctional epithelium without cementum or bone without cementum. No significant six-week histometric advantage for GMSCs was reported.
evidence_records.independent_unit: Seven dogs; multiple tooth sites are nested within animals, although the paper reports tooth as its analysis unit
evidence_records.sample_size: 56 tooth specimens across seven dogs; histometry available for 49 specimens
evidence_records.notes: Short-term canine histology does not establish human efficacy or a functional epithelial seal. Healing patterns were reported as unpredictable and not modified by added matrix or cells. No long-term recurrence or physiological load-transfer outcome.

evidence_records.source_title: Kulakov et al. 2021: early rabbit gingival augmentation histology
evidence_records.license: Primary article linked; this is an attributed summary without a source excerpt
evidence_records.model_system: Two collagen matrices with different placement approaches and local rabbit bone-marrow MSC administration
evidence_records.comparator: MSC injection versus no MSC injection; Mucoderm versus Mucograft
evidence_records.outcome: MSC administration was associated with higher early epithelialization and vascularization scores
evidence_records.measure: Semi-quantitative histology and immunohistochemistry at day seven
evidence_records.value: Reported MSC-associated epithelialization and angiogenesis differences p<.0001; matrix-dependent early epithelialization also favored Mucoderm over Mucograft
evidence_records.unit: Ordinal histology scores and vascularization measures
evidence_records.independent_unit: Twelve rabbits; multiple treatment conditions are nested within the animal experiment
evidence_records.notes: This is early soft-tissue augmentation, not recession coverage or root-to-periodontal attachment. Epithelialization morphology at seven days does not establish a durable seal, recurrence prevention or long-term gingival function.

evidence_records.source_title: Barootchi et al. 2019: twelve-year root-coverage follow-up
evidence_records.license: PubMed abstract record; full text was not retrieved for this review
evidence_records.stage_track: Twelve-year follow-up of a randomized clinical trial
evidence_records.model_system: Connective-tissue graft with or without epithelial collar; adjacent flap-only sites also assessed
evidence_records.comparator: CAF+CTG, CAF+epithelial-collar graft and adjacent CAF-only sites
evidence_records.outcome: Coverage declined in all groups; grafted sites showed less relapse than the adjacent flap-only sites
evidence_records.measure: Change in mean root coverage from six months to twelve years
evidence_records.value: Mean root-coverage decline 16.52% for CAF+CTG (p>.05), 19.42% for CAF+epithelial-collar graft (p<.05), and 34.12% for adjacent CAF-only sites (p<.05)
evidence_records.unit: Percentage-point change as reported by the source
evidence_records.independent_unit: Participants; recession sites are nested within the long-term follow-up cohort
evidence_records.sample_size: 17 of 20 original participants; 43 sites at twelve years
evidence_records.follow_up: Twelve years; compared with baseline and six months
evidence_records.notes: This is a clinical durability benchmark, not a cell-therapy study. It reports root coverage, not histologic attachment or a direct epithelial-seal assay. The long-term subset is small and site observations are nested within participants.

dental.title: Rat iPSC–BMP-6 hydrogel: defect signal with ankylosis tradeoff
dental.target: Orthotopic periodontal defect repair in a rat maxillary molar
dental.species: Male Sprague-Dawley rats and rat-fibroblast-derived iPSCs
dental.hypothesis: Local iPSC+BMP-6 hydrogel treatment can improve bone and histologic cementum/PDL formation in a rat defect, while ankylosis can coexist and functional attachment must be assessed separately.
dental.endpoint: Animal-level micro-CT bone measures, histologic cementum/PDL and ankylosis, and separately assessed oriented insertion, mobility, load transfer and durability.
dental.falsifier: Bone/mineral gain lacks a preserved ligament space, is accompanied by ankylosis, or fails to produce independent functional evidence on replication.
dental.study_design: Four-arm six-week rat defect study with animal as the independent unit; distinguish cell, BMP-6 and hydrogel effects and retain ankylosis as a competing outcome.
dental.structure_notes: Chien et al. (2018) report 16 male Sprague-Dawley rats in four groups (n=4/group), with rat-fibroblast-derived iPSCs plus BMP-6 hydrogel tested in a maxillary-molar defect. At six weeks the combination arm had the strongest reported bone micro-CT measures and new cementum/PDL histology. The paper also reports ankylosis in both BMP-6 arms. There was no iPSCs-only arm or direct load/mobility test; the six-week no-tumor observation does not establish long-term safety. This is not whole-tooth regeneration or human evidence. See IPSC_BMP6_RAT_DEFECT_REVIEW.md.

evidence.value: The rat iPSC+BMP-6 hydrogel arm showed new cementum/PDL histology and the strongest reported micro-CT bone measures at six weeks, while both BMP-6 arms could lead to ankylosis.
evidence.comparator: Control, hydrogel-only and BMP-6 hydrogel; no iPSCs-only arm
evidence.notes: Small animal study (n=4/group). Ankylosis and mineralized tissue are opposing outcomes for functional PDL restoration; no direct load-transfer or mobility endpoint was reported.

evidence_records.source_title: Chien et al. 2018: rat iPSC+BMP-6 hydrogel periodontal defect study
evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY 4.0; attributed summary
evidence_records.model_system: Maxillary-molar root-surface defect; four-arm comparison of control, hydrogel only, BMP-6 hydrogel, and iPSCs+BMP-6 hydrogel
evidence_records.comparator: Control, hydrogel-only, and BMP-6-hydrogel arms; no iPSCs-only arm
evidence_records.outcome: The combination arm had the highest reported micro-CT bone metrics and histology reported new cementum and PDL; the article also reports ankylosis in both BMP-6-containing arms
evidence_records.measure: Micro-CT bone-volume fraction, trabecular number/thickness; histology for cementum, PDL, and ankylosis
evidence_records.value: At six weeks the iPSC+BMP-6 hydrogel arm showed the strongest reported bone measures and new cementum/PDL histology, while both BMP-6-containing groups could lead to ankylosis

The paper reports ankylosis in both BMP-6-containing arms, so mineralized tissue does not establish a functional ligament space. No iPSCs-only arm, direct load/mobility test, or long-term safety follow-up. One blinded micro-CT assessor is reported; group randomization is not described in retrieved Methods. Authors reported no tumor or ectopic tissue during this short experiment, which does not establish long-term safety.

dental.title: PDL progenitor root preseeding: oriented reattachment signal
dental.target: Periodontal-ligament reattachment on denuded natural tooth roots
dental.species: Mouse PDL progenitors and athymic nude rats
dental.tissue: Natural molar root surface and periodontal ligament after tooth replantation
dental.hypothesis: Preseeding a denuded natural root surface with PDL progenitors can support oriented PDL formation and tooth retention after replantation, while resorption and ankylosis remain competing outcomes.
dental.endpoint: Root-level PDL histology and fiber orientation, tooth retention, resorption and ankylosis; directly measured mobility/load transfer must remain separate.
dental.falsifier: Preseeded teeth fail to sustain PDL and retention, or independent replication does not reproduce oriented insertion without increased resorption or ankylosis.
dental.study_design: Four athymic nude rats and eight replanted molars (four progenitor-preseeded, four cell-free); the source states six months in the abstract/Methods but six weeks in one Results sentence.
dental.structure_notes: Dangaria et al. (2011) report mouse PDL progenitors preseeded onto denuded rat molars before replantation. Histology describes polarized, parallel-oriented new PDL fibers; all four preseeded teeth reportedly retained physiological occlusion without root resorption, while two of four cell-free controls were lost and the remaining two resorbed/ankylosed. Follow-up timing conflicts within the paper (six months in abstract/Methods; six weeks in Results). Teeth are nested in only four athymic rats; there is no direct mobility or load-transfer assay. This is not iPSC-derived, chronic periodontal-defect or human evidence. See PDL_PROGENITOR_ROOT_PRESEED_REVIEW.md.

evidence.value: Four progenitor-preseeded replanted molars reportedly formed a new PDL with oriented fibers and retained physiological occlusion without observed resorption; two of four cell-free controls were lost and the remaining two resorbed/ankylosed.
evidence.unit: Tooth-level outcomes nested within four athymic rats
evidence.timepoint: Follow-up conflict: abstract/Methods say six months; one Results sentence says six weeks
evidence.notes: Cross-species mouse PDL progenitors on rat natural roots; replantation model, not iPSC construct or periodontal-disease defect. Occlusion was described, but direct mobility, bite-force and load-transfer measurements were not reported.

organoids.title: Ameloblast RNA comparisons and biological-unit gaps
organoids.species: Human-derived organoid RNA samples and a mixed fetal/iPSC reference
organoids.tissue: Ameloblast organoid transcriptome; functional enamel remains separate
organoids.hypothesis: Within-background molecular responses may support a maturation hypothesis after sample identity and independent culture provenance are qualified.
organoids.endpoint: Descriptive source-aligned CPM panel with library omission and pseudocount sensitivity; independent biological-unit qualification before inference
organoids.falsifier: Misaligned samples, unresolved clone or batch confounding, ambiguous tissue labels or a claim of a full factorial interaction without untreated-KO samples
organoids.evidence_stage: Retrieved public counts and computational descriptive comparison; tissue identity/function unqualified
organoids.study_design: Three source conditions with two labeled replicates each; genotype-by-treatment interaction is incomplete
organoids.structure_notes: GSE307437 supplies 41,129 unique gene rows in six source-aligned libraries. Descriptive CPM comparisons retain sparse enamel-associated rows and mixed molecular responses. Donor/clone/culture identities and reuse rights remain unqualified. Untreated KO is missing, so no full factorial interaction is estimated. GSE184749 pooling/tissue-label issues remain. See studies/dental-regeneration-2026-10-09/AMELOBLAST_EXPRESSION.md. Normalization diagnostics and per-library plots are in RNA_CONTEXT.md. Clone-to-library mapping remains unresolved after selected supplement review; major marker directions persist under two scalings.

evidence.notes: Source-aligned counts analyzed descriptively; molecular changes do not certify functional tissue identity.
Expression and source labels cannot supply native enamel mechanical function.

findings.boundary: Fifteen of 21 recruited patients completed the study. Attrition and endpoint-specific uncertainty need review; nonsignificance is not equivalence.

findings.claim: The 2016 trial reported bone-height improvement in both groups without a significant between-group difference.

findings.title: Dental RNA directions persist under two normalization methods
findings.claim: Total-count and median-ratio normalization retain major DLX3/SP6/SOX2 directions and within-condition nearest-library pairing; magnitude and sparse-marker discrepancies remain visible.
findings.boundary: Unknown donor/clone/culture independence, composition-sensitive normalization and missing untreated KO prevent causal interaction or donor-heldout claims. Expression does not establish native enamel or tooth function.
